report.tagline: A UK app-only bank with the hot coral card, known for a friendly app that makes managing money simple, and now solidly profitable.
report.simpleSummary: Monzo is a bank that lives in your phone. You get a bright coral debit card, instant notifications when you spend, and 'Pots' to put money aside for bills or holidays. It started as a prepaid card in 2015, grew through word of mouth and crowdfunding, and became a full UK bank. After years of losses, it now makes good profits, mainly from interest, card fees, loans and paid plans.

overview.whatItDoes: Monzo offers UK current accounts, savings, loans, overdrafts, credit cards (Monzo Flex), investments, pensions and business accounts, all in an app. Its strength is design: clear spending insights, instant alerts and tools that help people budget.
howItWorks: Open an account in the app in minutes with a photo ID and selfie video.
Get a coral card; every payment shows up instantly with the shop's logo.
Use Pots to save for goals and pay bills, and 'Salary Sorter' to split pay automatically.
Get paid a day early with Get Paid Early, and round up spending into savings.
Borrow with loans, overdrafts or Monzo Flex (buy now, pay later style).
Pay for Extra, Perks or Max for features like better savings rates, Railcard, travel insurance and phone insurance.
overview.valueProposition: Banking that is easy, friendly and helps you feel in control of your money.

businessModel.summary: Monzo earns mostly from interest: on loans and overdrafts, and on customer deposits it holds. It also earns card interchange fees, subscription fees from paid plans, and fees from business accounts. Low costs from an app-only model, and growth through word of mouth, helped it become profitable.

revenueStreams.detail: Interest from loans, overdrafts and Flex, plus interest on deposits held at the Bank of England.
Fee paid by shops each time customers pay by card.
Extra (£3), Perks (£7) and Max (£17) a month.
Insurance, investments and pensions through partners.

businessModel.pricing: Personal: free standard account. Extra £3 a month, Perks £7, Max £17. Business: free plan and paid plans. Loans and overdrafts at interest rates based on credit. Prices from monzo.com.
costDrivers: Regulatory costs, including a £21 million FCA fine in 2025 over financial crime controls
businessModel.unitEconomics: With about 14 million customers and £1.7 billion revenue, Monzo earns roughly £120 a year per customer. Profit before tax of about £172.6 million is about £12 per customer. A customer with salary in, a loan and a Perks plan may be worth several hundred pounds a year; a free user who only splits bills earns little. Getting more customers to use Monzo as their main bank is the key to profit.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth and the eye-catching coral card
Paying friends and splitting bills pulls in new users
Community forum and crowdfunding that built loyal fans
Marketing campaigns and growing brand trust
whatBringsUsersBack: Salary paid in, often a day early
growth.moat: Monzo's moat is brand love and habit. Millions of UK users check it daily, have salaries paid in and use Pots, which makes switching painful. Its community and friendly tone are hard to copy. Its licences and low-cost tech help too.

northStar.metric: Number of customers using Monzo as their main account (salary deposited monthly)
northStar.why: Main-account users trust Monzo with their money and use more products. This north star metric is a clear sign of value and drives revenue. Guardrail metrics make sure growth does not come at the cost of trust, safety or margins.

pmLessons: Delight can drive growth. Instant notifications and a coral card got people talking.
Community builds loyalty. Monzo's early fans helped shape and spread it.
Profit comes from depth. Getting salaries and loans matters more than sign-ups.
Compliance is not optional. Weak controls led to a fine.
Expansion is hard. Monzo's US push struggled, so Europe must be planned carefully.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you get more Monzo users to switch their salary?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find barriers: trust, hassle, features. Ideas: Get Paid Early, switching rewards, better savings. Measure salary deposits.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Monzo launch mortgages?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare value, risk, cost and capital. Consider partnerships. Measure products per customer.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce account freeze complaints?
interviewQuestions.hint: Balance fraud control and experience. Better communication and faster reviews. Track complaints and fraud.

interviewQuestions.question: Design Monzo's launch in Spain.
interviewQuestions.hint: Target users, local needs, competition, rules. Use community and design. Define metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Monzo's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Main-account customers. Break into new users, salary switching, products and trust.
